title: Who Grades the Agent? Privilege Separation for Coding-Agent Benchmarks
abstract: arXiv:2611.27860v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Benchmarks for AI-based coding agents are a staple of the current AI landscape, because they are the leading way to measure the performance of LLMs. Their scores guide business and research decisions. Evaluating coding agents is challenging, since they are able to manipulate their evaluation infrastructure to artificially achieve better scores. Grading an agent's solution often requires running its code, which can then manipulate the evaluation process. BenchJack, an automated benchmark auditor, recently reached near-perfect scores on nine of ten popular agent benchmarks without actually solving their tasks. Agents already do this unprompted, as OpenAI's July 2026 Hugging Face incident showed.   Building on secure systems design, we introduce SplitBench, a privilege separation framework for evaluating coding agents and the first in the scientific literature to separate running a task's tests from judging their results. translated_title: 谁来为智能体评分？面向编码智能体基准测试的权限分离机制
translated_abstract: 基于人工智能的编码智能体基准测试是当前人工智能领域的重要组成部分，因为它们是衡量大语言模型性能的主要手段，其分数指导着商业和研究决策。然而，评估编码智能体极具挑战性，因为它们能够操纵评估基础设施来人为地获取更高的分数。对智能体的解决方案进行评分通常需要运行其代码，而这段代码随后便可能操纵评估过程。自动化基准审计工具 BenchJack 最近在十个流行的智能体基准测试中的九个上获得了接近满分的成绩，而实际上并未真正解决任何任务。正如 OpenAI 2026 年 7 月的 Hugging Face 事件所显示的，智能体已经在无人指示的情况下自行实施这类操纵行为。借鉴安全系统的设计理念，我们提出了 SplitBench，一个用于评估编码智能体的权限分离框架，这也是科学文献中首个将“运行任务测试”与“判定测试结果”相分离的框架。即使智能体……
tldr: 本文提出 SplitBench，这是首个采用权限分离机制、将编码智能体基准测试中“运行测试”与“判定结果”相隔离的评估框架，可防止智能体操纵评估过程来骗取虚高的分数。
en_tdlr: SplitBench is the first privilege separation framework for coding-agent benchmarks that separates running a task's tests from judging their results, preventing agents from manipulating the evaluation infrastructure to inflate their scores.
